item.title: The Collins D.C. Council Report: Black History Unfolding in the Wilson Building in Real Time
item.description: The D.C. Council unanimously approved a ceremonial resolution honoring the late Donna Lorraine Wright-Miller, a social worker and holistic healer, and the Gardner Bishop Elementary School Redesignation Act of 2025, which would rename a school in honor of Gardner Bishop, a local civil rights leader. The post The Collins D.C. Council Report: Black History Unfolding in the Wilson Building in Real Time appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Trump Signs Funding Measure, Ending Partial Shutdown as DHS Fight Looms
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a funding measure that ended a four-day partial federal government shutdown, restoring operations across most federal agencies and sending furloughed workers back to their jobs, while setting up another confrontation over immigration enforcement and Department of Homeland Security funding later this month. The post Trump Signs Funding Measure, Ending Partial Shutdown as DHS Fight Looms appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: D.C. Students Lead Walkout Against ICE
item.description: Hundreds of Howard University students, along with students from other local campuses, marched from Franklin Park to the White House to protest ICE-led violence and operations, emphasizing the importance of collective action and intergenerational collaboration. The post D.C. Students Lead Walkout Against ICE appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: One Hundred Years Down, More to Go: ASALH Reflects on Centennial of Black History Month
item.description: The 100th anniversary of Black History Month is being celebrated by the Association for the Study of African American Life and History (ASALH) with a commitment to preserving and promoting the history and legacy of African Americans, despite the efforts of some to erase it. The post One Hundred Years Down, More to Go: ASALH Reflects on Centennial of Black History Month appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: D.C. Attorney General Secured Nearly $907 Million for District in 2025: Report
item.description: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) released its 2025 Impact Report, which details a year of litigation, enforcement, and legal defense that produced $906.8 million in savings and benefits for the District, a return of more than four times the office's annual budget. The post D.C. Attorney General Secured Nearly $907 Million for District in 2025: Report appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Zona Maco: Navigating the Imprint of Blackness in Latin America
item.description: At Zona Maco, Black and Afro-Mexican narratives remain largely peripheral, but Sean Kelly Gallery has worked to highlight Black artists in the Mexico City market and beyond, while Magola Moreno's paintings suggest that Black presence in Latin America does not always announce itself as a category or claim. The post Zona Maco: Navigating the Imprint of Blackness in Latin America appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Heart Awareness Month and the Fight for Equity in Cardiac Care
item.description: Despite advances in cardiovascular care, African Americans still die at higher rates from heart disease than their white counterparts, and the Association of Black Cardiologists is working to address this disparity through initiatives such as the Cardiovascular Desert Initiative and increased education and screening programs. The post Heart Awareness Month and the Fight for Equity in Cardiac Care appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Community Conversation Explores Pros and Cons of AI
item.description: AI has the potential to drive positive change, but its high energy demand and potential environmental implications must be carefully considered to ensure responsible usage and data center development. The post Community Conversation Explores Pros and Cons of AI appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: UDC at 175: A Legacy Celebrated, a Mission Renewed
item.description: The University of the District of Columbia (UDC) is celebrating its 175th anniversary with initiatives to boost student enrollment, foster workforce development, and raise funds for scholarships, all in an effort to become the District's key workforce engine and a national model for public education. The post UDC at 175: A Legacy Celebrated, a Mission Renewed appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Trump Sparks Firestorm With Racist Obamas Video, Removes Post After Backlash From Allies and Critics
item.description: President Donald Trump quietly removed a racist video from his social media account after fierce condemnation from across the political spectrum, following his overnight repost of a clip depicting former President Barack Obama and former first lady Michelle Obama as apes. The post Trump Sparks Firestorm With Racist Obamas Video, Removes Post After Backlash From Allies and Critics appeared first on The Washington Informer.
